exposure: Mode of delivery (TOLA2C vs ERCS vs TOLA1C)
Trial of labor after two previous caesarean sections (TOLA2C)
Elective repeat caesarean section following two caesarean sections (ERCS)
Trial of labor after one caesarean section (TOLA1C)
trial of labour after two previous caesarean sections (TOLA2C)
elective repeat caesarean section following two caesarean sections (ERCS)
trial of labour after one caesarean section (TOLA1C)
cohort: Pregnant women with singleton pregnancies who underwent TOLA2C (n=146), ERCS (n=206), or TOLA1C (n=99) at two regional obstetric centres between 2013 and 2021
finding: TOLA2C was associated with a 65% success rate and a greater risk of endometritis/sepsis, longer hospital stay, lower Apgar scores, and higher neonatal unit admission compared to ERCS and TOLA1C.
mod_finding: Trial of labor after two previous cesarean sections (TOLA2C) was associated with a greater risk of endometritis and/or sepsis postnatally, longer maternal hospital stay, a greater proportion of neonates with Apgar scores less than 7, and higher rates of neonatal unit admission compared to elective repeat cesarean section or trial of labor after one cesarean section.
